questions.prompt: Match each part of the cell to its job.
Found in plant cells only, or in both plant and animal cells?
questions.explain: Plant cells have three extra parts.

questions.prompt: Why don’t onion peel cells have chloroplasts, even though they are plant cells?
options: The onion bulb grows underground, where there is no light for photosynthesis
Chloroplasts are too small to see
questions.explain: Only plant cells exposed to light (like leaf cells) have many chloroplasts.

questions.prompt: Under the microscope you see regular, brick-shaped cells with thick outlines and green dots inside. What are they?
questions.explain: Cell walls and chloroplasts show they are leaf cells.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between the cell membrane and the cell wall?
options: The membrane is thin and controls what passes in and out; the wall is a tough outer layer (only in plants) that gives support
The wall controls entry; the membrane gives support
Animals have walls; plants have membranes
questions.explain: Plant cells have both: the wall outside the membrane.

questions.prompt: Give three differences between a plant cell and an animal cell, and explain why plants need each extra part.
questions.modelAnswer: 1) Plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which gives support so plants can stand upright without a skeleton. 2) Many plant cells have chloroplasts, which make food by photosynthesis, since plants cannot eat. 3) Plant cells have a large central vacuole filled with cell sap, which keeps the cell firm and stores water. Animal cells lack these, but have a flexible shape.

questions.text: The ___ is the control centre of the cell. The jelly-like substance around it is the ___.
questions.explain: Most chemical reactions happen in the cytoplasm.
